label: JZ Mock E · Paper 2 · Question 6
knowledgePattern: Test universal claims about a quadratic vertex locus
solution:
Complete the square: fb(x)=(x−b)2+c−b2. Its vertex is Pb=(b,c−b2). Eliminating b gives the locus y=c−x2, so I is false.

For II, the x-coordinate does increase with b, but the y-coordinate need not decrease. For example, b1=−2<b2=−1 gives heights c−4<c−1, so the second vertex is higher, not lower. Thus II is false.

A repeated root requires the minimum height to be zero: c−b2=0. Since c>0, the two distinct choices b=±c both work. III is false. None is necessarily true: answer H.

hints.title: Find the vertex coordinates
hints.body: Complete the square in x. Read the coordinates of Pb from the result.
hints.recap: Completed-square form shows the turning point directly.
hints.pitfall: Keep the sign of the constant term after completing the square.
hints.pause: Write the vertex as a coordinate pair.

recall.reminder: Completed-square form shows the turning point directly.

hints.title: Use the vertex formula to test the claims
hints.body: For the movement claim, try two negative values of b in increasing order. For the repeated-root claim, find when the vertex lies on the horizontal axis.
hints.recap: A universal claim must work for negative inputs as well as positive ones.
hints.pitfall: Keep both signs when solving an equation for a square.
hints.pause: Decide which statements survive these checks.
